correctness.rationale: Each projective point contributes a maximal twin class of \(q-1\) nonzero scalar multiples. The quotient neighborhood of a point is its polar line, with the point adjoined exactly in the isotropic case, so graph automorphisms recover the line structure and the orthogonal polarity. This yields \(\operatorname{P\Gamma O}(3,q)\) on the quotient and arbitrary symmetric permutations inside fibers. Twin transpositions give the lower bound \((q^2+q+1)(q-2)\) for both invariants; selecting all but one vector in every fiber attains both bounds. The packaged checker verifies the quotient automorphism counts, twin partition, diameter, and resolving construction for \(q=3,5\).

value.rationale: The theorem completely describes symmetry and resolving complexity for a natural archive-era algebra graph family. The full automorphism group retains nontrivial projective semilinear orthogonal geometry while the exact determining and metric dimensions are governed by scalar twin fibers. The coincidence of the two invariants, together with the exact classification and count \((q-1)^{q^2+q+1}\) of minimum sets, gives a reusable structural template rather than an isolated numerical computation.
